trust_decision.summary: When a config value whose schema type is [array, string] (args, node_args, ignore_watch, ...) arrives as a string, Config._valid tokenises it with a backtracking regex split; nothing bounds the cost of that split on untrusted config/CLI input.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Config.js and the string-to-array split regex; it is the only array-split regex in the file and in lib/.

fix_sites.entry_point: pm2 start <script> / pm2 start ecosystem.json / restart|reload --update-env via API._startScript, API._startJson, API.actionFromJson, API._handleAttributeUpdate -> Common.verifyConfs -> Config.validateJSON -> Config._valid; also public Config.validateJSON

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No separate route exists to dismiss: every caller funnels into the single split at lib/tools/Config.js:203 via Common.verifyConfs (lib/Common.js:844).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Quoted-argument grouping must keep working: key="v a", key='v', "a b" and 'a b' stay single tokens and plain whitespace-separated words still split; a naive \s+ split or quote rejection breaks args/node_args strings.

O7_producer.where: lib/API/schema.json:38-53 (types [array,string] select the split branch, loaded by the getter at lib/tools/Config.js:23-55)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: opts.only filter parsed with a split regex; a maintainer could have extended it to quoted app-name parsing with the same alternation idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same string-to-list job on CLI input in another file; would be a planted where-type copy, so it only counts as an extra.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: editor command string split into argv; a quote-aware tokeniser copied from Config.js would be plausible
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Also tokenises a user-provided command line; still a where-type planted copy.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an input length cap before the split, or replace it with value.split(/\s+/), which breaks quoted-argument grouping.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/API/pm2-plus/auth-strategies/CliAuth.js:278 has a nested-quantifier email regex applied to interactive login input; this is a separate input and feature, not pursued.
lib/tools/Config.js:185 compiles sch.regex from schema.json; the schema regexes (lib/API/schema.json:115,239,257) are linear and not attacker-controlled.
